mission.brief: Two fictional filesystems cannot accept new files. Save the two data rows of space.txt in space-report.txt and the two data rows of inodes.txt in inode-report.txt, without headers. Match by filesystem and mount, not row position. Display both sources and both final reports with cat after all writes. Self-review the constrained resource and safe next investigation for each; do not perform cleanup.
constraints: SIMULATOR: supplied synthetic snapshots of fictional hosts, not measurements of your computer or VM. No free, vmstat, df, processes, mounts, repairs or cleanup commands are simulated here.

Score checks factual report bytes, reading evidence and preserved sources only. Interpretation, uncertainty and recommended next checks require self-review; 100/100 is NOT proof of diagnostic mastery.

Type help for supported text commands. For this lab's context, worked interpretation and common mistakes, read HELP.txt with cat. This reference is available in both modes; it contains no repair command.

Only declared report files can be written. > truncates before reading; >> appends. Errors do not undo writes. Finish all report writes before reading sources and final reports: any actual write clears earlier reading evidence.

Keep source record spelling, units, order and final LF exactly in reports. Equivalent supported paths and filters count for report construction. Required reading evidence specifically uses cat on each source and final report after the last write; other tools do not satisfy cat inspections. Reasoning is self-reviewed. Reset preserves history.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR HELP — space versus inodes
These are supplied synthetic df -P -k and df -P -i subsets. 1024-blocks/Used/Available are block-space fields; Inodes/IUsed/IFree count inode resources. Two tables refer to the same fictional filesystems at the same time. These names are NOT devices available for commands.
Self-review: identify the limiting resource in each filesystem. What would you inspect before choosing cleanup or capacity expansion?
Model interpretation: archive has zero available blocks but many free inodes; spool has many available blocks but zero free inodes. A new ordinary file usually needs both. Confirm actual errors, filesystem type, reserved capacity and workload before acting. This fixture simplifies allocation/reservation details and does not model real exhaustion or recovery.
Common mistakes: using space percent as inode percent; mismatching mount rows; deleting arbitrary files; assuming a successful mount proves write capacity.
Automatically checked: two accurate reports, their readings and both original readings after final writes, preservation. Diagnosis/recommendations are self-reviewed. No rm, df, mount or repair is implemented in this contract. Type help for supported text tools.
Required checked reading actions use cat on each source and final report after the last write. Other text tools may construct reports but do not satisfy these cat actions.
